elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: §21.1 as rendered: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of ..." plus the retained sentence "The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims." No residual language leaves Customer uncapped.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered §21.1 reads "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000." The amount, basis and USD 1,000,000 floor match, but the temporal anchor is the event giving rise to the claim, not "the 12 months preceding the claim" required by this element; per the boundary rule those anchors are not equated (deterministic check "preferred cap lookback precedes the claim" = false).

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained §21.2: "Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill ..." — bilateral by its terms.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: §21.3 Excluded Claims (excepted from the §21.1 cap) includes "a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Same Excluded Claims definition expressly lists "data-protection, or security obligations"; §21.1 opens "Except for Excluded Claims".
§21.3: "its indemnification obligations" is within Excluded Claims, which sit outside the cap.
§21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" listed as Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: §21.3: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" within Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Rendered §21.3 final sentence, as amended: "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed amounts due for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section." The operation replaced the illusory defined term "Fees" (Implementation Fee only, §§1.5-1.6) with "amounts due", so the carve-out now reaches Customer's payment obligations generally; the retained "undisputed"/"for conforming Services" qualifiers are pre-existing Customer-favourable limits that were correctly not deleted. The deterministic flag on this item is triggered by wording, not by a substantive gap in coverage of Customer's payment obligations.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: §21.1 "each Party's total aggregate liability ... The cap is mutual"; no one-sided or unlimited-Customer language remains.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: §21.1 as rendered ties the cap to "the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim", with a USD 1,000,000 floor; the fallback element requires only a 12-months-of-fees basis and no particular temporal anchor. The "first Order Form" limitation and the illusory defined term "Fees" (USD 12,000 Implementation Fee) no longer drive the cap.
§21.3 Excluded Claims includes "its indemnification obligations", carved out of §21.1.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: §21.3 Excluded Claims includes "breach of confidentiality ... obligations".

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback level: the cap is mutual, is now based on twelve months of fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms (with a USD 1,000,000 floor), and indemnities, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct remain uncapped Excluded Claims.

Preferred level is one element short: the cap lookback runs from "the event giving rise to the claim" rather than "the 12 months preceding the claim" as the preferred element states. To reach preferred, amend §21.1 to read "during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim" (or otherwise anchor the lookback to the claim itself); every other preferred element is satisfied.

The finding correctly identifies the underlying defect: the original cap was pegged to "Fees" = the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, i.e. below the six-months'-fees walk-away floor, so "deviation" at critical severity is the right classification.

Minimality holds: only the cap basis in §21.1 and the noun in the §21.3 payment carve-out were touched. The USD 1,000,000 floor and "all Order Forms" are required by the chosen preferred checklist and to escape the first-Order-Form limitation respectively; the mutual cap sentence, the direct-damages sentence in §21.2, the "legally excludable" qualifier and the "undisputed"/"conforming Services" limits were all retained, and no extras (survival tails, procedures, damages categories) were added.

Intent preserved: no defined term was disturbed, no cross-reference dangles, and no retained sentence contradicts the new cap. One drafting note for the next turn (not a defect): §§1.5-1.6 still define capitalised "Fees" narrowly, so consider "all fees paid or payable" or a bracketed clarification that the cap is not limited to the defined term, to remove any capitalisation-based ambiguity; the USD 1,000,000 floor already prevents the cap from being illusory in any event.
